notes: Account background: mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics for mobile apps). Heavy emphasis on fast in-app support and query autocompletion. Product team owns vendor eval; platform/infra owns deployment constraints.

Use-case detail: primary = support-agent (context-window 2k tokens), secondary = embeddings for semantic-search (vector DB), occasional reranking for search results. Expected peak QPS: 35-45 queries/sec after ramp; avg request size ~600 tokens.

Latency & throughput targets: target median latency <150ms for interactive chat path, p95 <350ms. Throughput target for Dedicated: steady 25k tokens/sec equivalent across pool (approx). Cost sensitive: CTO flagged target TCO reduction of 40% vs hosted price at projected volume.

Security/compliance: must have SOC2 + SSO (SAML) + audit logs. EU data residency requirement for a subset of users (legal wants explicit routing/blocking). Prefer VPC deployment in Dedicated; fallback to Hosted for non-sensitive traffic.

POC takeaways: Hosted API good for early QA but token costs blow up at 1M+ monthly tokens. Demo of Dedicated runtime showed ~30% token-cost reduction in lab. Greystone wants committed baseline to guarantee latency and cost predictability.

Pricing convo notes (high level): Redwood proposed three committed tiers (Small / Mid / Large). Greystone is pushing for Mid tier with burst to 2x commit for 30 days/month. They asked for overage cap and blended token price if using fallback hosted models. Negotiation points: effective overage rate, minimum monthly commit ramp, and guaranteed burst window per month.

Specific commercial preference (from CFO): prefer a 6-month ramp: month1 30% commit, month2 60%, month3 80% then full by month4. Want calendar-based true-ups quarterly, not monthly, to smooth billing volatility.

Requested contract items: explicit SLA for latency (p99) on Dedicated routes, credit formula, dedicated maintenance windows, and a clause for model upgrades/compatibility (no surprise breaking changes).

Talked numbers - note for AE: Greystone indicated comfort with ARR in range $120k-240k if Redwood provides 30-40% cost reduction vs hosted and burst guarantees. CFO requested a worked example: committed tokens/day -> price -> monthly invoice -> predicted savings vs hosted (attach to proposal).
Quote from Head of Product: "We need predictable bills. If we get a hard committed baseline and a safe burst, we can justify moving traffic off hosted and lock in a dedicated pool."

SE notes (Jordan): Need to confirm kernel/quantization profile used in Dedicated quote (we priced using q4-int8 profile). Confirmed that model variants used for fallback must be explicitly mapped for routing to avoid sudden quality regressions.

Operational ask: want routing policy: primary route -> Dedicated pool (vpc), fallback -> Hosted-compatible variant with lower-cost quantization. Also asked about prefix/KV cache transfer semantics during failover (we need to document cache warm-up time).

Legal/security follow-ups: Greystone needs KMS integration details (customer-managed keys preferred), proof of SOC2 cert + recent audit report, and EU data residency appendix drafts. SE to provide technical KMS doc; security to provide SOC2 copy.

Internal redlines Greystone requested: limit on overage to 25% of commit/month before auto-escalation; ability to pause burst if spend exceeds a hard cap; clearer definition of what constitutes "burst" (sustained vs spiky).

Next internal action items for AE: produce three committed-tier proposals with explicit ramp schedules, example invoices, and a short appendix describing burst mechanics + overage calc. Ask finance to provide a blended price schedule for hybrid routing (dedicated + hosted fallback).

Greystone counter-requests: cap overage to 25% of committed monthly tokens before renegotiation; reduce overage rate to $8 per 1k for reranking/embedding endpoints; blended price for mixed model routing.
Billing preference: quarterly true-up, invoice in USD, option to convert to annual committed contract after 6 months with retro credit if thresholds met.
